argument:
Eaton's organic demand and improved $1.188bn H1 FCF validate operating merit, but debt rose from $9.895bn to $20.611bn against only $695m cash/investments. Acquisition payments of $11.079bn required external funding. Integration now must earn adequate returns on a much larger financing burden while segment margin has already fallen 80bp.

The bull's backlog offers a route to servicing acquisitions, not proof that those acquisitions create shareholder value. At 27.40x forward earnings, the price requires profitable delivery; adjusted EPS removes $1.04 of costs and guided GAAP EPS is nearly flat. Undrawn liquidity is not cash. Strong growth can make the exposure manageable, but quantified leverage and adjustment-heavy profitability offset upside more directly than generic macro support or an overbought uptrend can resolve.
key_points: Debt more than doubled through acquisition funding.
Margins compressed and adjusted/GAAP growth differ.
Premium forward valuation requires profitable integration.
rebuttal_to_previous: Improved operating FCF is the bull's strongest evidence, but it is small beside $11.079bn acquisition payments and doubled debt. Backlog must produce returns after financing rather than simply enlarge reported sales.
